notes:
Summary: SMB ecommerce storefront building chat-first returns and order-triage assistant. Early inbound, self-serve trial. CTO Priya Rao technical lead. Wants hosted API (public cloud only) — no VPC/on-prem. Primary concerns: rate limiting behavior under marketing-driven traffic spikes, predictable quotas for engineers, and clear guidance on handling 429s. Target metrics shared by customer: baseline throughput ~100 req/s, median response latency target 200-400ms, expected promo spikes up to 3-4x baseline for 4-8 hours. They ran a smoke test and saw 429s at ~180 concurrent connections; also saw burst token cost spike when users paste long chat histories.

What they asked for:
- Clear concurrency + per-minute quota numbers for hosted_api SKUs
- Example backoff and jitter strategy for 429s (prefer code snippets in Node/Python)
- Recommendations for streaming vs non-streaming for lower tail latency during spikes
- Cost estimate for allowing higher burst windows vs steady-state commit

What we proposed:
- Send sandbox keys and a short "Rate Limits & Burst Handling" tech note with sample retry policies
- Suggest enabling prefix KV caching for repeated context to reduce token load
- Recommend 1) soft quota raise for trial, 2) guide on exponential backoff + capped retries, 3) advice on batching user inputs where appropriate

Quotes / color: "If we get 429s during a marketing push, it's a showstopper — we can't tolerate customer-visible failures" — Priya Rao (CTO). Team is technical and will test quickly. They appreciate simple docs and sample code. Cost-sensitive; want to understand per-chat economics before committing.
